intro: On 10 August more than 600,000 people called on the EU to defend its nature laws while wildfires moved across Europe. The four months from September put that argument into four rooms almost at once, UNGA, CBD COP17, UNFCCC COP31 and BBNJ COP1, and what separates four parallel efforts from one coherent position is largely planning discipline: a single view of the milestones, an honest reading of what is at risk, and someone holding the actions between meetings. That is the contribution I am offering as the independent consultant for this assignment, and it is the work I have done for the last six years inside organisations facing the same problem on a different subject.
experiences: My background is in coordinating regulatory and policy programmes that cut across functions, organisations and borders. At the Global Reporting Initiative I chaired a 53-member consortium spanning corporates, government bodies and NGOs across five countries. At CDP Worldwide I was the primary point of contact for more than 150 disclosing organisations through a full reporting cycle and supported delivery of the CDP-hosted workshop in Warsaw. At TUI AG, a DAX-listed group, I built and steered a cross-functional project team carrying new regulatory obligations into operation across international subsidiaries. I now work as an independent contractor, determining the methodology, tools and delivery approach for each engagement and reporting progress against agreed milestones.

skills.name: Integrated Project Frameworks, Risk and Dependency Management
skills.body: The first deliverable asks for a consolidated framework across four policy moments, with milestones, dependencies and delivery risks in one place. That is the shape of the CSDDD and LkSG programme I ran at TUI AG, where the obligations landed at once on Compliance, Risk, Legal, IT and supply chain, across international subsidiaries at very different levels of readiness and with no single plan for any of it. I built and steered a cross-functional project team, set the deliverables and the dates, mapped which workstream could not start until another finished, and held contributors to their deadlines without line authority over one of them. Alongside the plan I maintained the trackers and completion records entity by entity, and wrote the process documentation and decision-rights splits establishing who owned each requirement. Senior leadership could then see progress and slippage by entity rather than in aggregate, risks surfaced early enough to be mitigated rather than reported after the fact, and the documentation held up when audit partners reviewed it as assurance evidence.

skills.name: Multi-stakeholder Coordination and Convening
skills.body: The assignment turns on coordinating people who do not report to the consultant, across Programmes, Communications, Public Affairs, Digital, Development and the CEO's Office. That was my position at the Global Reporting Initiative, where the consortium ran to 53 members across corporate, government and civil society mandates in five countries, and positions on any given question rarely started in the same place. I chaired the recurring meetings, set the agendas, facilitated between competing views and carried every action through to closure rather than into the next meeting. Between sessions I issued member newsletters and policy updates on regulatory developments, convened speaker-led sessions with industry associations and policymakers, and presented GRI Standards at the Bombay, Colombo and Dhaka stock exchanges. Members who began from opposing positions reached agreed outcomes, the consortium kept one authoritative record of what had been decided and by whom, and the evaluation of 53 members against 17 SDGs was completed rather than stalling in disagreement.

extraParagraphs: My coordination work has been delivered from inside organisations and around convenings rather than on the floor of a UNFCCC or CBD negotiation, so the multilateral setting itself would be new to me. The mechanics the assignment specifies are not: readiness assessments against a plan, briefing schedules, action and decision logs, status reporting to a lead, and a lessons-learned review that changes how the next one is run. I have built each of those, and the policy substance, EU climate regulation, UNFCCC outcomes and national commitments, is material I have followed and written on throughout.

On the practical terms: I am based in Berlin and would contract through ClientEarth gGmbH in Germany, I am available for the four days a week the assignment requires from mid-September through to 31 January, and I can travel for on-site support at COP31 in Antalya. My financial proposal and CV, including a list of engagements and clients, are attached.
closing: I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how this background could add value to the Global Public Affairs and Policy team through what will be an unusually concentrated four months.
